analysis: Examined the three changed files. StatusCommand.swift (head lines 135-140) now derives a display-only authorization via state.displayedProviderAuthorization(...) and keeps a separate removalAuthorization from the strict currentProviderAuthorization(...). Both are passed to ProviderAuthorizationReadiness.summary(authorization, removalAuthorization:, now:). The strict path is unchanged, so the MDM-removal gate is not loosened in this diff. UnenrollCommand+KeepServing.swift (head lines 23-27) still gates on removalReady(authorization, now:) using the strict currentProviderAuthorization, and only the error message now uses the new summary signature with removalAuthorization: authorization. The re-read just before offering removal (head lines 61-67) is untouched, which preserves the T-053 and T-057 posture that stale authorization must not enable premature MDM removal. The added test (StatusCommandRunTests.swift lines 253-279) asserts that an unexpired lease with a late renewal still shows App Attest in status, while removal text says it needs fresh coordinator readiness and does not say 'removal is available' or suggest unenroll. The change affects only local CLI display and does not touch the coordinator wire, keys, or authorization grant. Remaining unverified contracts, which are outside the supplied evidence: the implementations of displayedProviderAuthorization and ProviderAuthorizationReadiness.summary(removalAuthorization:). Reviewers should confirm that displayedProviderAuthorization still enforces coordinator URL binding and lease expiry, and that summary only says 'removal is available' when removalAuthorization is non-nil and removalReady. Status output is informational only, so impact is limited to misleading messaging if those contracts are wrong.
